title: QUIC RFC 9000 ECN Packet-Number-Space Separation
purpose: Describe the focused S13.4.1 ACK-generation boundary that keeps acknowledgment state and ECN counts separate for each packet number space.
design_summary: ACK-generation state is partitioned by QUIC packet number space. Recording an ECN-marked processed packet updates only the acknowledgment set and ECN counters for that packet number space. Building an ACK frame for another packet number space cannot borrow packet numbers or ECN counters from the populated space, and identical numeric packet numbers in Initial, Handshake, and Application Data spaces remain independent entries with their own ECN counter totals.
data_and_state_considerations: The same numeric packet number can exist in multiple packet number spaces. The ACK-generation state therefore treats packet number space as part of the state key for both acknowledgment ranges and ECN totals.
edge_cases_and_constraints: An empty packet number space does not produce an ACK frame because another space contains ECN-marked packets.
Identical packet numbers in different packet number spaces produce ACK frames with separate ECN counts.
The focused proof covers ACK-generation state separation, not ECN validation of peer ACK frames.
risks: This slice does not claim ECN validation correctness for ECT(0), ECT(1), or ECN-CE deltas.
This slice does not claim coalesced-packet ECN accounting.
This slice does not claim endpoint interop success.

supplemental_sections.heading: Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: This design closes the focused ACK-generation ECN separation proof for REQ-QUIC-RFC9000-S13P4P1-0006 only. ECN validation and coalesced-packet counting remain under separate traced requirements.
